title: A CGI multiplexer makes every script in one directory reachable, including the forgotten ones
index_line: T-0061 · EXEC · one endpoint dispatches to any CGI in a shared directory; a legacy script still calls the shell · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: Reachability is assumed to be the same as being linked: if the interface offers a function, a script exists for it. But a multiplexer that dispatches by name over a shared directory exposes every script in it — including the ones for features that were removed, whose code was never hardened because the feature was gone. The dispatcher is the attack surface; the directory is the catalogue.

mechanism.does: the attacker requests the shared CGI entry point with a parameter naming a different script
the multiplexer normalises the name and dispatches to the corresponding file in the shared directory
a legacy script runs, still holding the input handling it had when its feature was supported
a request field reaches a shell invocation built by string concatenation
the command executes as the web server's account, which on the appliance is root

source.http.request.value: the dispatcher parameter naming the script, plus the script's own parameter

sink.exec.shell.value: the legacy script's shell call built from a request field

encoding.shell.value: metacharacters accepted by the old handler, which few filters guard

guard.none.value: no authentication on the dispatcher and no input validation in the legacy script

preconditions.expr: the device or app is reachable and the CGI directory is served
a shared dispatcher exposes multiple scripts by name
a legacy script places a request field into a shell command

success: a script reachable only through the dispatcher executes a command from a request field
the device returns command output or a side effect with no authentication
the dispatcher's own page does not mention the script — it is reachable only by name
failure_like: the dispatcher restricts names to a table of known-good scripts
the legacy scripts were deleted with the feature
false_positive: a 404 for the script name — the dispatcher refused it
a page that echoes the parameter into HTML without executing it

hazards: enumerate the CGI/plugin directory and request every file through the dispatcher; the ones the UI never calls are the interesting ones
appliance firmware is the usual home: one busybox CGI tree shared by several generations of the UI
these handlers predate input validation as a practice, so metacharacter payloads work without cleverness
related to T-0060 (orphan pages found by path): here the dispatcher is the catalogue, so the discovery is a name, not a directory listing
non_transfers: dispatchers restricted to an explicit name-to-handler table
modern frameworks routing every request through one controller

evidence.target: Digiever DS-2105 Pro 3.1.0.71-11, time_tzsetup.cgi via cgi_main.cgi (CVE-2023-52163)
